aiExplanation: This function figures out the fewest **rotations** (plus an optional **reversal**) needed to turn `nums` into a sorted ascending array, treating the array as a circle. It first scans every pair of neighbours, including the wrap-around pair at the end, looking for a **break point** `bp` where `nums[i] > nums[i + 1]`. If exactly one such drop exists, the array is a rotated sorted list: when the drop sits at the very last index the array is already sorted and the answer is `0`, otherwise the answer is the cheaper of rotating left `bp + 1` times or rotating right the remaining distance. If two or more drops are found, `bp` is set to `-2` and the function repeats the same scan in the opposite direction, searching for a single spot where `nums[i] < nums[i + 1]`, which would mean the array is a rotated **descending** list. If that also fails it returns `-1` because sorting is impossible; if it succeeds it returns the minimum rotation count for the descending arrangement plus `1` extra operation to reverse the array into ascending order.
